text:
maria: FYI customer 'Pecan Health' reported weird duplicated invoice numbers after we merged their LoRA into redwood/semantix-base-7b-merged and quantized to 4-bit.
linh: Ugh. Any sample prompts/responses?
josh: Pushed a quick eval pack to the workspace. Short summary: on 1000 invoices, 4-bit model repeats numeric substrings in ~2.7% vs 0.1% on float16. Token-level odds skewed around token ids 450-520.
alex: Could be tokenizer or kv-cache corruption. Did we use the customer's tokenizer or our default? Pecan used pecan-v2-tokenizer.
maria: They provided an example. Paste: "Invoice # 00456 paid on 2024-01-09" -> model returns "Invoice # 00456 00456 paid ..."
sophie: Can you run the quick smoke with tokenizer=pecan-v2 and also with `--kv-check=true`?
josh: Running now. Command I used:
```
redwood-eval run --model redwood/semantix-base-7b-merged:loRA-pecan --quant awq-4bit --prompt-file pecan-quickset.json --tokenizer pecan-v2 --out results.json
```
josh: Early results: with pecan-v2 tokenizer + awq-4bit, duplication drops to 0.9%. With default HF tokenizer + awq it's 3.1%.
linh: That's a strong signal for tokenizer mismatch. Still higher than float16 though.
alex: Another angle: different quant kernels handle attention softmax scaling slightly differently. Try `--kernel=ggml-smooth` vs `--kernel=awq-native`.
maria: Also try re-running with `--prefix-cache=false` to rule out prefix/KV caching interaction. If duplication only when cache enabled that's a routing bug.
josh: I ran both kernels. ggml-smooth + pecan-v2 => 0.4% duplicates. awq-native + pecan-v2 => 0.9%.
sophie: Interesting. So two orthogonal contributors: tokenizer mismatch and kernel numerical behavior.
devops-bot: Model redwood/semantix-base-7b-merged:loRA-pecan routed to dedicated-gpu-pool-3 for these evals. Avg latency @32B tokens = 48ms.
maria: Action items: (1) confirm ingest uses pecan-v2 tokenizer end-to-end, (2) add tokenizer alignment test to quickpack, (3) flag default kernel to ggml-smooth for this LoRA until we ship kernel-fixes.
linh: I'll add a tiny unit test to the LoRA onboarding CI that runs 50 synthetic invoice prompts and asserts duplicates < 1% (token-level dedup check).
josh: I'll prepare a short note for customer explaining temporary mitigation: use pecan-v2 tokenizer and prefer ggml-smooth. Also include the quick eval artifact link: https://redwood-internal/runs/1751239999/pecan-quick
alex: Also file a runtime bug: attention-scaling diff between awq-native and ggml-smooth when sequence length > 128. Might be kv cache scaling.
sophie: I'll update the quick-eval pack with tokenizer param and a mini README.
maria: Thanks team. Ping me when CI test merged and we have a concise customer message. :pray:
josh: CI patch in draft: https://git.redwood/loRA/onboard/pulls/42 — includes test and a reproducer script.
linh: I'll review the PR after lunch.
maria: Great — if anything else pops I'll update this thread.
